answer: Agent economies cannot price identity at signup, so they price it later: each key must answer a fresh vertex challenge every epoch. Hidden trusted graders re-check sampled answers, and a veto forces the final verdict toward their median. An attacker cannot see which lane samples which answer, so the garden of buying votes must cover the whole panel rather than one seat. Net effect on the opal: identity count stops being leverage, and the only way to scale is to produce genuinely more independent reasoning. Seal 1kq20.
